title: Sebastian's Cotton Club and the Les Hite band
summary: He recalls the Cotton Club house band with Lionel Hampton and Louis Armstrong recording, Hampton as the only drummer allowed, and the floor shows.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Don't have too many of those anymore. You said you mentioned you went to Sebastian's Cotton Club while you were out here. Who was in Les Hite's Heidt's band then?
Lionel Hampton. Marshall Royal. Let's see, Lawrence Brown, and of course Louis Armstrong came in there, you know, and did all the recording with that

But Lionel -- with every band that came in there, even when Earl Hines came in there later, they made Earl leave his drummer out, and Lionel had to -- Frank Sebastian said, 'No, there's only one guy plays drums in this place, and that's Lionel.'
Rather upsetting, you know, if you walked in with Gene Krupa or somebody in your band, and you'd say, 'Wait a minute, we've got our own drummer.'
Well, they were like the house band at --

Yeah. They had had these big shows there. Like Timmy Rogers, I remember him, he was in the show there, and they didn't have any -- they didn't go in for any names, but they had the chorus line and oh, they had singers and comedians, and it was quite a colorful place. Of course the gambling room was upstairs.
